title: Open redirect from request parameter
description: sendRedirect / Location header fed from getParameter (CWE-601).

title: Java file path from variable
description: new File / FileInputStream / Paths.get with a non-literal argument (CWE-22 path traversal heuristic).

title: JAX-RS sensitive @Path
description: @Path for admin/api/internal/manage/console — confirm @RolesAllowed AUTHORIZATION.

title: JAX-RS @PermitAll (public/UNAUTHORIZED)
description: @PermitAll on RESTEasy/JAX-RS resource — endpoint is explicitly unauthenticated.

title: Spring Security anyRequest//** permitAll
description: UNAUTHORIZED: Spring allows all URLs without authentication (anyRequest or /** permitAll).

title: Spring sensitive URL permitAll
description: UNAUTHORIZED sensitive path (admin/api/actuator/console/internal) marked permitAll — should be AUTHORIZED.

title: DESKeySpec weak key material
description: new DESKeySpec — DES is cryptographically weak

title: Empty TrustManager checkServerTrusted
description: checkServerTrusted(...) { } — empty trust check disables cert validation

title: Insecure Random in security context
description: java.util.Random used near token/session/password/otp/nonce variables

title: Symmetric key built from a hardcoded string literal
description: SecretKeySpec constructed from a literal string means the encryption/JWT-signing key ships in the source and in every built artifact. Rotate it and load from environment or a secrets manager. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: SSLContext with obsolete SSL protocol
description: SSLContext.getInstance("SSL") — protocol too old; use TLSv1.2+

title: Cipher IV derived from the key material
description: The CBC/GCM initialisation vector is built from the key (or password/secret) bytes, so it is static across every encryption. A fixed IV defeats CBC entirely and is catastrophic for GCM — derive the IV from SecureRandom per message and store it alongside the ciphertext. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: HostnameVerifier always returns true
description: HostnameVerifier verify method returns true unconditionally (CWE-295).

title: Weak cipher DES/AES-ECB
description: Cipher.getInstance uses DES or AES/ECB (CWE-327).

title: Cipher ECB mode
description: Cipher algorithm string includes /ECB/ (CWE-327).

title: Weak MessageDigest algorithm (MD5/SHA-1)
description: MessageDigest.getInstance("MD5"|"SHA-1"|"SHA1")

title: Broken password-based encryption (PBEWithMD5AndDES)
description: PBE scheme combining MD5 with single/triple DES. Both primitives are broken and the KDF iteration count is far below modern guidance — use PBKDF2WithHmacSHA256 or Argon2 with AES-256. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: JSch StrictHostKeyChecking disabled
description: JSch/SSH session configured with StrictHostKeyChecking=no — accepts any host key, enabling MITM on SFTP/SSH connections. Generalized from a legacy-audit pattern (regex_data/NPG-SECURITY_SCAN_PATTERNS.md).

title: Drools rule resource loaded from a variable path
description: addResource/newFileSystemResource called with a non-literal path — if that path is externally influenced, arbitrary rule logic could be injected into the KIE session. Generalized from a legacy-audit pattern (regex_data/NPG-SECURITY_SCAN_PATTERNS.md).

title: Reflection Class.forName with variable
description: Class.forName(variable) — reflection with potentially user-controlled input

title: HTTP header set from request input
description: Response header written from getParameter/getHeader (CWE-113 HTTP response splitting / reflected CORS).

title: LDAP filter with string concatenation
description: InitialDirContext / DirContext search with concatenated filter argument

title: ProcessBuilder with string concatenation
description: new ProcessBuilder(...) with concatenated argument — command injection risk

title: Java Runtime.exec command execution
description: Runtime.getRuntime().exec(...) — OS command injection risk (CWE-78)

title: ScriptEngine.eval dynamic script
description: ScriptEngine.eval usage (CWE-94 code injection).

title: XSS via JSP/servlet output of request data
description: response.getWriter().write or out.println writing request-sourced data

title: Request data written straight into a JSP
description: A scriptlet expression or Struts <bean:write> emits request/parameter data into the page. Unless the tag escapes by default (Struts 1 <bean:write> only does with filter="true"), this is reflected XSS. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Uploaded file type decided from the filename string
description: The upload's type is derived by slicing the client-supplied filename, with no MIME or magic-byte check. An attacker renames a payload to .jpg and the server accepts it — validate content, not the name, and never reuse the original name on disk. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Exception object set into a REST response DTO
description: .setException(ex) on a status/response DTO — if that DTO is later serialized into the HTTP response body, the client receives the full stack trace and internal class names. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPG-*.md, regex_data/NPC-*.md).

title: Exception message returned directly in HTTP response body
description: ex.getMessage()/FieldError.getDefaultMessage() passed into a ResponseEntity .body()/.ok() call, or set on a response DTO's message/error field via a builder or setter (e.g. ErrorResponse.builder().message(ex.getMessage())...build(), later returned via new ResponseEntity<>(dto, status) — not just the .body()/.ok() fluent form) — directly, or first assigned to a local variable and returned a few lines later (the most common GlobalExceptionHandler/@ControllerAdvice idiom). If unescaped, this reflects exception text (which can carry a rejected field value from a validation failure, or internal class/stack detail) straight into the HTTP response, enabling reflected XSS or information disclosure.

title: Unsanitized exception/request data logged directly
description: logger call embeds ex.getMessage(), request.getRequestURI()/getRequestURL()/getQueryString(), or a raw request.getParameter()/getHeader() value directly — anywhere in the call's argument list, not just the first argument (parameterized logging with multiple args, e.g. log.warn("... {} {}", request.getRequestURI(), ex.getMessage()), is the common real-world shape). If the underlying value carries attacker-controlled newlines or control characters, this enables log injection/forging (CWE-117): forged log entries, fake timestamps, or corrupted log parsing. Distinct from java-sensitive-data-in-logs (keyword-based secret detection) and logger-exception-tostring (info-disclosure from discarding the stack trace, not injection).

title: Exception logged via toString() instead of the exception object
description: logger.error/warn/info/debug(..., ex.toString()) — coercing the exception to a string discards the stack trace and can expose internal class names/paths in log output without the diagnostic value a real exception argument would give. Generalized from a legacy-audit pattern (regex_data/NPG-SECURITY_SCAN_PATTERNS.md).

title: Struts 1.x FormFile upload handling
description: Struts 1.x FormFile has no built-in content-type or size validation, and the framework is end-of-life. Review the surrounding code for magic-byte validation, a size cap, and a server-generated storage name. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: CORS Allow-Origin from request or wildcard
description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin set to * or from request input (CWE-942 permissive CORS).

title: CORSFilter reflects Origin header
description: Access-Control-Allow-Origin set from getHeader("Origin") — UNAUTHORIZED unless allowlist-checked first.

title: Cookie created — verify setSecure/setHttpOnly
description: new Cookie(...) — confirm nearby .setSecure(true) / .setHttpOnly(true)

match:
Cookie c = new Cookie("sid", id);
response.addCookie(c);

title: DocumentBuilderFactory without XXE hardening nearby
description: DocumentBuilderFactory.newInstance — confirm FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING / external-entity disable is set nearby

title: SAXParserFactory without XXE hardening nearby
description: SAXParserFactory.newInstance usage (CWE-611). Confirm disallow-doctype-decl / external entity features are set.

title: XMLInputFactory without XXE hardening nearby
description: XMLInputFactory.newInstance — confirm external entity / DTD support is disabled

title: JAX-RS ContainerResponseFilter CORS headers
description: ContainerResponseFilter adding Access-Control-Allow-Origin — confirm allowlist AUTHORIZATION.

title: RESTEasy CorsFilter allowedOrigins *
description: JBoss RESTEasy CorsFilter getAllowedOrigins().add("*") — all origins AUTHORIZED for CORS.

title: Servlet Access-Control-Allow-Origin *
description: setHeader/addHeader Access-Control-Allow-Origin to * in servlet/filter code.

title: Servlet CORSFilter class (javax/jakarta)
description: Hand-written Servlet Filter named CORSFilter — review Allow-Origin allowlist (JBoss/Tomcat, not Spring-only).

title: Auth exception message built from concatenated user input
description: UsernameNotFoundException/BadCredentialsException message is built by concatenating the submitted identifier. If this message reaches an HTTP response or is distinguishable from a wrong-password error, it enables username/email enumeration.

title: isEnabled() grants login to a non-active/pending status
description: UserDetails.isEnabled() (or similar account-status check) returns true for a status containing PENDING, alongside the active status — unverified/onboarding accounts can authenticate before activation completes.

title: Config lookup falls back to a hardcoded credential
description: A credential/secret is read from config with a literal default, so the application still starts — with a known password — when the setting is missing. Require the value explicitly and fail closed. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Session expiry disabled or set extremely high
description: setMaxInactiveInterval(-1) disables session expiry entirely; a five-digit value is over 2.7 hours. Long-lived sessions extend the window for hijacking. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Castor XML deserialization
description: org.exolab.castor.xml (Castor) in use — its Unmarshaller performs type-confusion-prone XML deserialization and the library is long EOL. Generalized from a legacy-audit pattern (regex_data/NPG-PAK-SECURITY_SCAN_PATTERNS.md).

title: Jackson polymorphic default typing enabled
description: Default typing makes Jackson instantiate classes named in the JSON itself, turning any deserialized untrusted document into a gadget-chain entry point (the Jackson equivalent of the commons-collections chain). Use explicit @JsonTypeInfo with a closed allow-list. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Java insecure deserialization (ObjectInputStream)
description: new ObjectInputStream(...) — flag especially when .readObject() follows

title: Java insecure deserialization (XMLDecoder)
description: new XMLDecoder(...) — insecure deserialization sink

title: Serializable class without serialVersionUID
description: A class implements Serializable with no serialVersionUID declared nearby — worth a look if a vulnerable deserialization gadget-chain library (e.g. an old commons-collections) is also on the classpath. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Exception silently swallowed
description: An empty catch block discards the exception, so the failure is invisible to logging and monitoring — a security-relevant error (failed authz, crypto error) leaves no trace. Log it or rethrow. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Stack trace printed instead of logged
description: printStackTrace() writes to stdout/stderr, bypassing the logging pipeline — the trace is missing from centralised logs and may surface to the client on some containers. Use logger.error("msg", e). Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Database error codes read for propagation
description: SQLState/vendor error codes describe the schema and database product. Returning them to a caller hands an attacker a fingerprinting and SQLi-tuning oracle — log them server-side and return a generic error. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Debug output written to stdout/stderr
description: System.out/System.err writes bypass the logging pipeline and its redaction, so whatever is interpolated (often request or user data) lands unfiltered in container output. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: Hardcoded localhost or file: endpoint
description: A loopback or file: URL baked into source. Beyond being environment-specific, these leak deployment paths and often mark a spot where an endpoint should have been configurable and allow-listed. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPC-*.md, regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: URL/URI from request parameter
description: new URL/URI built from getParameter (CWE-918 SSRF heuristic).

title: SSRF via config-sourced SOAP/HTTP endpoint
description: A URL/URI or SOAP endpoint reference (setTargetEPR/EndpointReference) is built from a config property value — verify the property's source can't be externally influenced, or that the resolved host is checked against an allowlist. Generalized from legacy-audit patterns (regex_data/NPG-*.md).

title: SQL built by string concatenation
description: A SQL statement or WHERE/SET clause literal is concatenated (or appended) with a variable. Unless the value is strictly validated, this is SQL injection; use a PreparedStatement with ? placeholders or named parameters.

match: String sql = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + userId;
String q = "delete from orders where id=" + id;
String q = "SELECT a FROM t" + " WHERE " + condition;
String q = String.format("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = %s", id);
query = "UPDATE account SET balance = " + amount + " WHERE id = " + id;
no_match: log.debug("select from cache failed for " + key);
logger.info("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = " + id);
String sql = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?";
String sql = "SELECT * FROM t WHERE x = " + TABLE_NAME;
throw new IllegalStateException("Cannot select from " + name);
// String sql = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = " + userId;

title: prepareStatement/prepareCall argument built by concatenation
description: The SQL passed to prepareStatement/prepareCall is concatenated, so the PreparedStatement does not protect it; bind values with ? placeholders instead.

match: ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = " + id);
no_match: ps = conn.prepareStatement("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ?");

title: Statement executes a SQL string held in a variable
description: A java.sql.Statement executes SQL passed in as a variable. Check how the string is built; if any part is user-controlled, switch to a PreparedStatement.

title: JPA/Hibernate query built by concatenation
description: A JPQL/HQL/native query string passed to createQuery/createNativeQuery/createSQLQuery is concatenated. Use named or positional parameters (setParameter) instead.

match: em.createQuery("from User u where u.name = '" + name + "'");

title: JdbcTemplate SQL built by concatenation
description: SQL passed to a JdbcTemplate/NamedParameterJdbcTemplate method is concatenated. Pass values as arguments with ? or :name placeholders.

match: jdbcTemplate.queryForList("SELECT * FROM t WHERE name = '" + name + "'");

title: ORDER BY / GROUP BY column taken from a variable
description: A sort or group column is concatenated after ORDER BY / GROUP BY. Placeholders can't bind identifiers, so map the requested column against an allow-list.

match: String q = base + " group by " + field;

title: OS command built by concatenation
description: The command passed to exec() is concatenated with a variable. A shell metacharacter or extra argument in that value becomes command injection; pass a fixed String[] argv and validate each value.

title: ProcessBuilder runs a shell with -c
description: ProcessBuilder starts sh/bash/cmd with -c (or /c), so the next argument is parsed by a shell. Any variable in it is command injection; run the program directly with separate arguments.

title: SpEL expression parsed from a variable
description: parseExpression() is called with a non-literal expression. If any part comes from a request, it is expression-language injection (remote code execution); never evaluate user-supplied SpEL.

title: EL value expression created from a variable
description: createValueExpression() receives a non-literal expression string. User-controlled EL is expression-language injection.

title: XPath expression built by concatenation
description: An XPath expression is concatenated with a variable. Quote characters in the value change the query (XPath injection); use XPathVariableResolver or strict validation.

title: JNDI lookup of a non-constant name
description: A naming context looks up a name held in a variable. If that name can be influenced by a user, it is JNDI injection (remote class loading on older JDKs).

title: Reflective method lookup by a variable name
description: getMethod/getDeclaredMethod resolves a method name held in a variable. If the name is user-controlled, a caller can invoke arbitrary methods; map names against an allow-list.

title: Template source evaluated from a variable
description: A template engine evaluates template *source* held in a variable. User-controlled template text is server-side template injection (often RCE); only render templates from trusted files.

match: Template t = new Template("x", new StringReader(source), cfg);

title: File path taken from a request/DTO getter
description: A file is opened from a value returned by a getter such as getFileName()/getPath(). When the object comes from a request this is path traversal; resolve against a base directory and reject '..'.

title: File path built by concatenating a separator and a variable
description: A file path is concatenated from a directory, a separator and a variable. Without normalizing and checking the result stays under the base directory, '../' in the value escapes it.

title: Request parameter used as a file path
description: A @RequestParam/@PathVariable String flows into a File/Path constructor in the same method. That is path traversal unless the value is validated against an allow-list or a canonical base directory.

title: JAX-RS parameter used as a file path
description: A @QueryParam/@PathParam/@FormParam String flows into a File/Path constructor in the same method — path traversal unless validated.

title: Redirect target taken from a variable
description: A Spring MVC redirect is built from a variable. If it comes from the request, it is an open redirect; only redirect to relative paths or an allow-list.

title: Exception message returned in a JAX-RS response
description: An exception's message is written into a response DTO or entity. Internal details (SQL, class names, paths) leak to the caller; return a generic message and log the detail.

title: Throwable stored on a response object
description: A Throwable is stored on a DTO via setCause/setThrowable/setStackTrace. When that DTO is serialized, the stack trace and messages reach the client.

title: Exception message passed to ResponseStatusException
description: The reason given to ResponseStatusException is an exception's message, which Spring can render back to the client.

title: Authorization decided from a request body field
description: A role/admin/permission flag is read from the @RequestBody object itself. The client controls that value; derive authorization from the authenticated principal instead.

title: Request body bound directly to a domain type
description: @RequestBody binds to a type that is not a DTO/request/form type. If it is a JPA entity, a client can set fields it should never control (id, role, owner); bind to a dedicated DTO.

title: CORS allows any origin together with credentials
description: A wildcard origin pattern is combined with allowCredentials(true), so any website can make authenticated cross-origin requests and read the responses.

title: @CrossOrigin open to every origin
description: @CrossOrigin with no origins (or origins = "*") lets any website call this endpoint from a browser. Name the allowed origins.

title: All Spring Boot actuator endpoints exposed over HTTP
description: management.endpoints.web.exposure.include=* publishes every actuator endpoint (env, heapdump, configprops, ...), which leak secrets and internals. Expose only health/info, or secure them.

title: H2 web console enabled
description: The H2 console gives a SQL shell (and, on older versions, code execution) to anyone who can reach it. Disable it outside local development.

title: Debug/trace output or stack traces enabled in config
description: debug/trace mode or server.error.include-stacktrace=always exposes internals in logs and error responses.

title: Spring Security ignores every path
description: web.ignoring() on /** removes the whole application from the security filter chain — no authentication, CSRF or headers.

title: Password compared in plain text
description: A password is compared with equals() against a stored value, which means passwords are stored unhashed (and the comparison is not constant-time). Store a salted hash (bcrypt/argon2) and use its matcher.

title: Cookie value taken straight from a request parameter
description: A cookie is created with a raw request parameter value — response splitting on old containers and cookie injection otherwise.

title: Content-Disposition filename from a variable
description: A download filename is concatenated into Content-Disposition without encoding. Quotes or CR/LF in it break the header (header injection, spoofed file names).

title: Bearer token extracted with indexOf + 7
description: The token is cut out of the Authorization header by offset instead of checking the header starts with 'Bearer '. A malformed header yields a wrong token or an exception.

title: JWT parsed without signature verification
description: parseClaimsJwt/parseUnsecuredClaims/JWT.decode read a token without verifying its signature; anyone can forge the claims. Use parseClaimsJws / a JWTVerifier.

title: JWT signing secret hardcoded in source
description: The HMAC key used to sign or verify JWTs is a string literal. Anyone with the source can mint valid tokens; load it from a secret store.

title: Encryption key derived from a string without a KDF
description: Key bytes are taken directly from a password/string (getBytes, truncated with Arrays.copyOf). That key has little entropy and no salt; derive it with PBKDF2/scrypt/argon2.

title: AES-CBC without authentication
description: AES/CBC gives confidentiality only; without a MAC an attacker can tamper with ciphertext (padding oracle). Prefer AES/GCM.

title: Cipher requested without a mode and padding
description: Cipher.getInstance("AES") (or DES/RSA) uses the provider default — ECB for AES, PKCS#1 v1.5 for RSA. Always name the mode and padding (AES/GCM/NoPadding, RSA/ECB/OAEPWithSHA-256AndMGF1Padding).

title: RSA without OAEP padding
description: RSA with PKCS1Padding or NoPadding is vulnerable to padding-oracle and malleability attacks; use OAEP.

title: Key generated with a weak size
description: An RSA/DSA/DH key of 1024 bits or less, or a 40-64 bit symmetric key, can be broken. Use RSA >= 2048 and AES-128/256.

title: Legacy sun.misc Base64 or a home-made XOR cipher
description: sun.misc.BASE64Encoder is an internal JDK class (removed in newer JDKs), and XOR 'encryption' classes are obfuscation, not encryption. Use java.util.Base64 and a real cipher.

title: Password stored as Base64
description: A password is Base64-encoded before being stored. Base64 is an encoding, not protection; hash passwords with bcrypt/argon2.

title: Password hashed with a plain message digest
description: A MessageDigest is used near password handling. A fast, unsalted digest (MD5/SHA-*) is cracked offline quickly; use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2/PBKDF2.

match:
MessageDigest md = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
byte[] h = md.digest(password.getBytes());
no_match:
MessageDigest md = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256");
byte[] h = md.digest(fileBytes);

title: Database credentials embedded in a JDBC URL
description: A JDBC URL carries a username/password (user/pass@host, //user:pass@host or password=...). Move credentials to a secret store or container-managed DataSource.

title: Cleartext protocol URL in source
description: A hardcoded http/ftp/telnet/ldap/t3 URL sends data (often credentials) unencrypted. Use the TLS variant (https, ftps/sftp, ldaps, t3s).

title: Plain (non-TLS) socket
description: A raw Socket/ServerSocket sends data unencrypted. Use SSLSocketFactory/SSLServerSocketFactory unless the channel is local-only.

title: LDAP bind with no or simple authentication
description: SECURITY_AUTHENTICATION 'none' binds anonymously; 'simple' sends the password in clear unless the URL is ldaps:// or StartTLS is used.

title: JAXB unmarshals a raw reader/stream
description: JAXB unmarshals directly from a reader, file or source rather than a hardened XMLStreamReader/SAXSource, so external entities may be resolved (XXE) depending on the implementation.

title: TransformerFactory without external-access restrictions
description: TransformerFactory.newInstance() is used without ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/STYLESHEET or FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING nearby, so a stylesheet or document can pull external resources (XXE/SSRF).

match:
TransformerFactory tf = TransformerFactory.newInstance();
Transformer t = tf.newTransformer();

title: SchemaFactory without external-access restrictions
description: SchemaFactory.newInstance() is used without ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD/SCHEMA restrictions nearby (XXE/SSRF via schema imports).

title: XMLReader created without disabling external entities
description: An XMLReader is created without disallow-doctype-decl / external-entity features nearby, so parsing untrusted XML resolves external entities (XXE).

title: Xerces DOMParser/SAXParser without disabling external entities
description: A Xerces DOMParser/SAXParser is instantiated directly without disallow-doctype-decl / external-entity features nearby (XXE).

match:
DOMParser p = new DOMParser();
p.parse(new InputSource(in));

title: XStream deserializes XML
description: XStream.fromXML on untrusted input has a long history of remote-code-execution gadgets. Configure an allow-list (allowTypes) or avoid XStream for untrusted data.

title: SnakeYAML default constructor on untrusted YAML
description: Before SnakeYAML 2.0, new Yaml() / new Yaml(new Constructor()) instantiates arbitrary classes from YAML tags (RCE). Use SafeConstructor or upgrade.

no_match: Yaml yaml = new Yaml(new SafeConstructor(new LoaderOptions()));

title: Kryo class registration disabled
description: setRegistrationRequired(false) lets Kryo instantiate any class named in the stream — a deserialization gadget surface.

title: SQL text written to a log
description: A SQL/query string is logged. Logged SQL can carry user data and reveals schema details; log a statement id instead.

title: java.util.Random inside a token/session/key generator
description: A method whose name says it produces a session id, token, nonce, OTP, salt or key uses java.util.Random/Math.random, which is predictable. Use SecureRandom.

title: Shared static SimpleDateFormat
description: SimpleDateFormat is not thread-safe; a static instance shared across requests corrupts dates under load. Use java.time.DateTimeFormatter.

match: private static final SimpleDateFormat FMT = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd");
no_match: private static final DateTimeFormatter FMT = DateTimeFormatter.ISO_DATE;

title: Deprecated SSL/TLS protocol version
description: SSLv2/SSLv3/TLSv1/TLSv1.1 are deprecated and broken (POODLE, BEAST). Use TLSv1.2 or TLSv1.3.

title: TrustManager accepts every certificate
description: getAcceptedIssuers returns null/an empty array, the signature of a trust-all TrustManager; certificate validation is effectively off (MITM).

title: Cookie Secure/HttpOnly explicitly disabled
description: setSecure(false)/setHttpOnly(false) sends the cookie over cleartext or exposes it to JavaScript.
